'''Monte Morris''' (born June 27, 1995) is an American [[college basketball]] player who played college basketball for the [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State Cyclones]].  

== Early life and high school career ==
Morris was born in Grand Rapids, Michigan and his mother is Lationa Morris.  His mother nicknamed him "Man-Man" when he was born.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/100285/iowa-states-morris-no-longer-little-man-man|title=Monte Morris no longer little Man-Man|publisher=}}</ref>  He grew up in [[Flint, Michigan]] attending Flint Beecher High School.  He was a four-year starter for the Beecher Buccaneers.  Morris was a three-time winner of Michigan's [[Associated Press]] Class C Player of the Year Award and a three time all-state selection.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://highschoolsports.mlive.com/news/article/7197031100801105393/flint-beechers-monte-morris-named-ap-class-c-all-state-player-of-the-year/|title=Flint Beecher's Monte Morris named AP Class C All-State Player of the Year|publisher=}}</ref>  He led the Buccaneers in scoring, assists, and steals in all four seasons.  He led Flint Beecher to back-to-back Class C Michigan state titles in 2012 and 2013.  One of the nation's best point guards, Morris won [[Mr. Basketball of Michigan|Michigan's Mr. Basketball]] award in 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://highschoolsports.mlive.com/news/article/-1378207149571926495/beecher-senior-monte-morris-wins-2013-mr-basketball-award-over-stellar-field-of-finalists-with-video/|title=Beecher senior Monte Morris wins 2013 Mr. Basketball award over stellar field of finalists (with video)|publisher=}}</ref>

He was ranked No. 96<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/player-Monte-Morris-112003|title=Rivals.com|publisher=}}</ref> in the final [[Rivals.com]] national rankings and No. 89 in the [[Scout.com]] ratings as well as being a [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://communitytable.com/14852/brianmclaughlin/meet-parades-2013-all-america-basketball-teams/|title=Meet PARADE's 2013 All-America Basketball Teams|first=Brian|last=McLaughlin|publisher=}}</ref>  Monte was recruited to [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]], [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]], [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]], [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]], [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]], [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]], and [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]] which he ultimately committed to.

== College career ==

=== Freshman season ===
Morris started the season on the bench  but worked his way into the starting line-up against the [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma Sooners]] February 1, 2014 staying there ever since.  Morris averaged 6.8 points, 3.7 assists and 2.6 rebounds and dished out 134 assists, the third most by any freshman in school history.  He shot 84.7 percent (61-72) at the free-throw line, the second-best mark by an ISU freshman and was the only Big 12 freshman to make at least 25 threes (28-69) and shoot over 40 percent.  He scored in double figures in 13 games, including all three games in the [[2014 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]]. Morris tallied a season-high 15 points in the Cyclones' NCAA Tournament win against [[North Carolina Central Eagles men's basketball|NCCU]] and followed that with 13 against [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]].  He dished out five or more assists in 12 games and led all Big 12 freshmen with 46 steals, the fifth most by an ISU rookie.  His 1.3 steals per game ranked seventh in the Big 12 and he had an ISU freshman record 12 assists with no turnovers against West Virginia.  He played 52 minutes of turnover free basketball in ISU's triple-OT win at [[Oklahoma State Cowboys men's basketball|Oklahoma State]] and had 10 points and five assists, including the game-winning 3-pointer with 43 seconds left in the third overtime against the Cowboys.  He broke the NCAA record and led the nation with a 4.79 assist-to-turnover ratio, including a 6.9 assist-to-turnover ratio in Big 12 play.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://amestrib.com/sports/men-s-basketball-morris-goes-overshadowed-budding-star|title=Men’s Basketball: Morris goes from overshadowed to budding star|publisher=}}</ref>

=== Sophomore season ===
Monte started all 34 games and averaged 11.9 points, second on the team.  He also posted a Big 12-best 5.2 assists and 3.4 rebounds on his way to earning All-Big 12 Second-Team honors.  He had second-most assists of any sophomore and 11th-most by any player in school history. Monte was second in the Big 12 in field goal percentage shooting 50.7 percent from the field, had 64 steals, the second-most by a sophomore and tied for the ninth-most by any player in a single season in school history.  His 110 steals in the last two seasons were the most by any Big 12 player.  His first-career 20-point game came against [[Texas Tech Red Raiders men's basketball|Texas Tech]], he recorded his first double-double and just missed a triple-double with 11 points, 10 assists and seven rebounds against [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://amestrib.com/sports/men-s-basketball-cyclones-power-way-past-jayhawks|title=Men’s Basketball: Cyclones power way past Jayhawks|publisher=}}</ref>  He tallied a career-high 24 points and hit buzzer-beating 17-foot fadeaway to beat [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] in Big 12 quarterfinals.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.si.com/college-basketball/2015/03/12/iowa-state-beats-texas-monte-morris-big-12-tournament|title=Watch: Monte Morris buzzer-beater lifts Iowa State over Texas in Big 12 tournament|first=SI|last=Wire|publisher=}}</ref>  He averaged 15.3 points to earn Big 12 All-Tournament team honors as the [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Cyclones]] won the [[Big 12 Men's Basketball Tournament|Big 12 Tournament]] for the second consecutive season and he did not commit a turnover in three games at the [[Big 12 Men's Basketball Tournament|Big 12 Championship]].  He led the nation for the second consecutive season with a 4.63 assist-to-turnover ratio and finished season with 176 assists and just 38 turnovers.

===Junior season===
On February 1, 2016, he was named one of 10 finalists for the Bob Cousy Point Guard of the Year Award.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Nortlander|first1=Matt|title=Cat Barber, Fred VanVleet missing from list of Cousy Award finalists|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/25468790/cat-barber-fred-vanvleet-conspicuously-missing-from-cousy-award-finalists|accessdate=February 2, 2016|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=February 1, 2016}}</ref> He was named to the 35-man midseason watchlist for the [[Naismith Trophy]] on February 11.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Payne|first1=Terrence|title=Naismith Trophy midseason list announced|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/oklahoma-sooners-buddy-hield-lsu-tigers-ben-simmons-naismith-trophy-35-finalists-021116|accessdate=February 19, 2016|work=[[Fox Sports]]|date=February 11, 2016}}</ref> 

===Senior season===
[[File:ISU vs Nevada (33115136630).jpg|thumb|right|Morris competing against Nevada in the NCAA Tournament]]
Morris received preseason recognition on November 2, 2016, as the [[Associated Press]] named him to the preseason [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] team.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/duke-s-allen-leads-ap-preseason-all-america-team-110216 |title=Duke's Allen leads AP preseason All-America team |publisher=[[Foxsports.com]] |date=November 2, 2016 |accessdate=November 12, 2016}}</ref> At the end of his senior season, Morris broke the NCAA record assist-to-turnover ratio from 4.79 he set his freshman year to the new record of 5.21. In 2017 Morris lead Iowa State to a 5th seed and got to the second round before losing to Purdue

===NBA draft===
Morris will participate in the 2017 NBA draft. He is a projected middle 2nd round pick or late first.
